digest:
The day’s new papers weave a rich tapestry around holography and conformal field theory, with several works sharpening the bridge between bulk geometry and boundary data.  A striking theme is the universal higher‑spin gap bound in large‑N CFTs, derived via a generalized brane‑interpolation picture and translated into holographic language.  This result not only constrains Planck‑scale separation in AdS vacua but also explains the bounded gaps observed in vector models.  Complementing this, the holographic test of entanglement cohomology in higher dimensions confirms the JLMS relation and shows that modular Hamiltonian perturbations encode the first entanglement cohomology class, reinforcing the deep link between bulk canonical energy and boundary relative entropy.  The non‑Riemannian holography paper further enriches this narrative by constructing an O(D,D)‑covariant dictionary that admits independent soft‑hair modes coupled to long strings, offering a new arena where boundary data and bulk dynamics intertwine.

On the CFT side, the strong‑generation proof for the chiral algebra of μ=4 SU(N) SYM organizes the infinite Schur spectrum into a finite set of supersymmetric multiplets, providing a concrete handle on higher‑point conformal blocks.  The explicit differential‑product construction for the on‑shell higher‑spin algebra in AdS_d supplies a practical tool for higher‑spin interactions, while the integrable deformation study maps η‑deformed sigma models to W‑algebra CFTs, extending the dictionary between integrable field theories and algebraic structures.  In the realm of number theory, the analytic quantum invariants work rewrites colored Jones polynomials as analytic (q,X)‑series, revealing unexpected links to mock modular forms and hinting at deeper L‑function and Langlands‑type structures.  Finally, the long‑range Ising CFT papers showcase how nonlocal critical points can be tackled with standard CFT techniques, offering a benchmark for higher‑point correlators in power‑law interacting systems.  Together, these results advance our understanding of holographic dualities, higher‑spin dynamics, and the algebraic underpinnings of conformal field theories, all of which resonate with the physicist’s interests in holography, celestial amplitudes, and the mathematical structures that support them.

papers.title: Light EFT Strings and Asymptotic Accelerated Expansion
papers.authors: Veronica Collazuol, Alessandra Grieco, Irene Valenzuela
papers.abstract: We study the interplay among towers of particles, EFT strings, and EFT membranes near perturbative infinite-distance limits of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories. We show that the scaling vectors of EFT membranes lie in the lattice generated by those of the EFT strings, as previously found for particle towers, and determine their specific relative scaling in F-theory and Type IIA Calabi-Yau compactifications. We then leverage these objects to assess the viability of asymptotic accelerated expansion in flux compactifications. While our bottom-up analysis does not yield a general obstruction, we rule out two candidate accelerating trajectories in F-theory because an EFT string becomes lighter than the Hubble scale, invalidating the four-dimensional EFT. This closes the loophole found in arXiv:2209.11821. We also study how recent results on quantum obstructions to $\mathcal{N}=1$ infinite-distance limits may provide a concrete resolution by changing the asymptotic form of the K\"ahler potential.
papers.summary: The paper investigates how EFT strings and membranes control the spectrum of towers near infinite‑distance limits in 4d N=1 compactifications, and uses this to test the possibility of asymptotic accelerated expansion in flux vacua. It finds that in F‑theory the lightest EFT string can become lighter than the Hubble scale, ruling out two previously suggested accelerating trajectories and closing a loophole in earlier work.

papers.title: Angular Momentum Loss at Fourth Post-Minkowskian Order
papers.authors: Alessandro Georgoudis, Carlo Heissenberg, Gustav Mogull, Rodolfo Russo
papers.abstract: We calculate the total loss of angular momentum for a gravitational scattering of two non-spinning point-like objects at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$. Our methodology combines use of both amplitudes and worldline-based methods. We derive the integrand from two copies of the gravitational waveform with cuts on massive lines arising naturally from the worldline. We then glue these two copies and evaluate the resulting phase-space integrals using reverse unitarity, in the amplitudes spirit. We obtain separately the radiated angular momentum and the static contribution that, at this order, is entirely determined by the initial shear and the linear memory. Combining these two terms, we derive relativistic expressions for the angular momentum loss and for the infrared-finite component of the mass dipole loss, which in the low-velocity limit match results available in the literature. We also use this result to derive the conservative deflection angle at $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$ and first self-force order.
papers.summary: This paper computes the angular momentum loss in a gravitational scattering of two non-spinning point masses at fourth post-Minkowskian order, combining amplitude and worldline techniques. The authors derive both radiated and static contributions, verify consistency with low-velocity limits, and use the result to extract a fifth-order conservative deflection angle.

papers.title: On the Positivity of de Sitter Group Averaging
papers.abstract: Perturbative quantum gravity about a global de Sitter (dS$_d$) background involves constraints that restrict the state of the linearized theory but which appear only at higher orders in perturbation theory. In particular, for familiar gravitational theories with $d>2$ these constraints require all charges defined by continuous de Sitter isometries to vanish in the linearized state. While standard Fock spaces have the property that the only normalizable state satisfying these constraints is the vacuum, Higuchi suggested that this lack of allowed states should be remedied by instead using the so-called group-averaging inner product. This inner product satisfies important uniqueness conditions, but its positivity has to date remained an open question. For $d > 2$, we establish this positivity here for all such states with $N$ particles (including particles of arbitrary spin) in standard global dS${}_d$ modes where the particle-weights $\Delta_i$ satisfy the condition ${\rm Re} \, \sum_{i=1}^N \Delta_i > d-1$, which is the criterion for group averaging to converge absolutely for arbitrary finite linear combinations of such states. We also treat the case of bosonic and fermionic (integer and half-integer spin) particles in dS$_2$ as a toy model for the more general case.   However, we can identify certain classes of states for which group averaging continues to converge absolutely for smaller weights. Interestingly, in some cases these smaller-weight states turn out to have {\it negative} group-averaging norms. We thus also discuss the implications of this observation for perturbative de Sitter quantum gravity.
papers.summary: The paper establishes the positivity of the group-averaging inner product for perturbative quantum gravity in de Sitter space, showing that all linearized states with sufficiently large total weight have non‑negative norms, while some lower‑weight states can acquire negative norms. It also discusses the implications of these findings for the consistency of de Sitter quantum gravity and the role of constraints in the linearized theory.

papers.title: Wrapping M5-branes on a non-spin manifold: Spin$^h$ structures and AdS$_7$ black holes
papers.authors: Okan G\"unel, Cameron Gibson, C. N. Pope
papers.abstract: We construct a solution of seven-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_5$, where $M_5$ is the five-dimensional Wu manifold $SU(3)/SO(3)$. The solution is supersymmetric, despite the fact that the Wu manifold admits neither a spin structure nor a spin$^c$ structure. Rather, it admits a spin$^h$ structure, wherein the ill-definedness of ordinary spinors due to a minus sign in their holonomy is compensated by a further minus sign arising through the spinors carrying $SO(3)$ Yang-Mills charge, in a half-integer isospin representation of the $SU(2)$ double cover of the $SO(3)$. We show how the configuration can be lifted to a solution of $D=11$ supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_9$, where $M_9$ is the unit tangent bundle of the Wu manifold. We discuss the geometry and topology of $M_9$, and study the supersymmetry from the eleven-dimensional standpoint. We extend the seven-dimensional solution to a black hole, and discuss some aspects of its holographic interpretation and the UV to IR flow. We revisit a previously-known AdS$_2\times H^3\times H^2$ solution, and its UV to IR flow, showing that the flow equations in fact admit of an exact solution. Additionally, we give a detailed discussion of the lift of the AdS$_2\times S^5$ solution to $D=11$, exhibiting similarities and differences between the properties of its internal space $M_9$ (the unit tangent bundle of $S^5$) and the Wu manifold example of our main discussion. We also construct the non-compact dual of the Wu manifold solution, where $M_5$ is taken to be $SL(3,\mathbb R)/SO(3)$.
papers.summary: The authors construct a supersymmetric AdS$_2	imes M_5$ solution of seven‑dimensional maximal gauged supergravity, where $M_5$ is the non‑spin Wu manifold $SU(3)/SO(3)$, and lift it to an eleven‑dimensional AdS$_2	imes M_9$ background with $M_9$ the unit tangent bundle of the Wu manifold, thereby exploring spin$^h$ structures and their holographic implications. They further extend the solution to a black hole, analyze its UV–IR flow, revisit an AdS$_2	imes H^3	imes H^2$ configuration, and compare with the $S^5$ case, highlighting the role of internal geometry in the dual quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Topological deformations of local gauge theories: a presymplectic BV-AKSZ approach
papers.authors: Ivan Dneprov, Alexey Donchenko, Maxim Grigoriev
papers.abstract: The same local degrees of freedom can be described by systems with different gauge structure and field content. Standard examples are the duality between the scalar field and the 2-form gauge field in four dimensions, and unimodular gravity, where the cosmological constant becomes a global degree of freedom. In a precise sense, the spaces of gauge-inequivalent formal solutions of such systems differ by a finite-dimensional sector. Moreover, because their gauge sectors are different, their consistent interactions and their sensitivity to the global structure of spacetime may differ substantially. We show that such systems are naturally related by what we call topological deformations: gauging a symmetry of generic degree couples the system to a BF-type sector without introducing new local degrees of freedom. The construction is carried out systematically within the presymplectic BV-AKSZ approach, where it amounts to a modification of the underlying presymplectic gauge PDE. Gauging degree-0 symmetries identifies solutions related by global symmetries, which reproduces the scalar--2-form and principal chiral model--Freedman--Townsend dualities. Gauging degree-1 symmetries, i.e. deformations, gives rise to new global degrees of freedom, such as the cosmological constant in unimodular gravity.
papers.summary: This work develops a systematic BV‑AKSZ framework for implementing topological deformations that couple gauge theories to BF‑type sectors without adding local degrees of freedom, thereby relating dual descriptions such as scalar–2‑form and principal chiral model–Freedman–Townsend dualities. It also shows how gauging higher‑degree symmetries introduces global degrees of freedom, exemplified by the cosmological constant in unimodular gravity.

papers.title: Gravitational Cheshire effect from Yang-Mills instantons
papers.abstract: We show that the dimensional reduction of four-dimensional Yang-Mills instantons naturally gives rise to nontrivial matter configurations in three dimensions exhibiting an unusual mechanism of gravitational screening. Starting from Euclidean Yang-Mills theory, we reduce (anti-)self-dual gauge configurations along a compact direction generated by a $U(1)$ isometry of the instanton background. Under this reduction, the gauge connection decomposes into a three-dimensional Yang-Mills field and an adjoint Higgs field, while the metric gives rise, as usual, to a dilaton and an Abelian gauge connection. For instantons on the Taub-NUT background, the reduced fields organize themselves into two mutually screening pairs: the backreaction of the Abelian sector cancels internally, and the same occurs independently in the non-Abelian sector. As a result, the full matter content supports a composite stealth configuration on flat three-dimensional space. By contrast, the dimensional reduction of instantons on the Eguchi-Hanson background yields a non-Abelian matter sector whose gravitational backreaction cancels, while the Abelian sector remains gravitationally active and therefore deforms the three-dimensional background geometry. These examples reveal a direct connection between four-dimensional (anti-)self-duality and three-dimensional BPS-type relations, and illustrate how instantonic sectors that are gravitationally invisible in four dimensions can descend into either fully composite stealth configurations or partially stealth matter configurations after dimensional reduction.
papers.summary: The paper shows that reducing 4D Yang–Mills instantons on Taub–NUT or Eguchi–Hanson backgrounds yields 3D matter configurations that can be fully or partially gravitationally stealth, revealing a link between 4D self‑duality and 3D BPS‑type relations. It demonstrates how instantonic sectors invisible in 4D can produce composite or partially stealth matter after dimensional reduction.

papers.title: Landscape of Higgs vacua in 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$
papers.authors: Amihay Hanany, Elias Van den Driessche
papers.abstract: Strongly coupled 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories have a Higgs branch of their moduli space of vacua, identified by 1/2-BPS operators and their algebraic relations. For $SU(N_c)_k$ theories, we map the moduli space across different phases and we establish how the Chern-Simons level $k$ deforms the chiral ring relations among mesons, baryons, and instantons, while determining specific patterns of symmetry enhancement. For $SO(N_c)$ theories, we construct the corresponding chiral ring constraints at infinite coupling. Finally, we identify the Higgs branch as a classical integrable system, through the expansion of the chiral ring in terms of action variables.
papers.summary: This work maps the Higgs branch of 5d N=1 SU(Nc)_k and SO(Nc) gauge theories, showing how the Chern‑Simons level deforms the chiral ring of mesons, baryons and instantons and leads to specific symmetry‑enhancement patterns. The authors further identify the Higgs branch with a classical integrable system by expanding the chiral ring in action variables.

papers.title: Covariant One-Loop Corrections from a Non-Covariant Expansion: The Scalar Field Case
papers.authors: Lucas Ducastelo de C. C. Lima, Riccardo Fecchio
papers.abstract: We compute the one-loop correction to the non-minimal coupling of a scalar field theory to gravity, induced by a quartic self-interaction. We adopt the non-covariant framework of linearized gravity and explicitly compute the corresponding Feynman diagram, including both the divergent and the finite parts. The corresponding contribution to the one-loop effective action is obtained by the requirement of covariance and compared with the known results obtained by the heat kernel technique. We study the running of the non-minimal coupling, its UV and IR limit and verify the validity of the decoupling theorem in the momentum subtraction scheme of renormalization. The linearized gravity approach is also used for deriving the effective potential for the scalar field and its covariant version is stated. The agreement with results derived using strictly covariant methods is verified and highlights the versatility of the linearized gravity approach.
papers.summary: The paper computes the one-loop correction to the non-minimal scalar–gravity coupling using a non-covariant linearized gravity expansion, deriving both divergent and finite parts and confirming covariance by comparison with heat kernel results. It also studies the renormalization group flow of the coupling and constructs the effective potential, demonstrating consistency with covariant methods.

papers.title: Bosonization for the Schwinger effect at small fermion mass: analytic formula for the 1+1D current in an arbitrary time-dependent, inhomogeneous electric field
papers.abstract: We derive an analytic formula for the expectation value of the current due to Schwinger pair-production in an arbitrary time-dependent, spatially inhomogeneous external electric field in 1+1 dimensions, as a perturbative expansion in the fermion mass $m$. We work to order $m^2$, finding contributions at order $m^0$, $m^2 \log m$ and $m^2$; there is no contribution at $O(m)$. The calculation is enabled by a new ``hybrid method'' using bosonization, where part of the calculation is performed on the fermion side and part is performed on the boson side. The fermion side allows us to define the vacuum using the free theory in the infinite past, while the boson side allows us to compute the current without regularization, since the current operator is linear in the boson field. In the special case of a spatially homogeneous background field, we also perform the calculation purely on the fermion side using adiabatic regularization. The detailed agreement of the results provides a highly non-trivial check of the duality.
papers.summary: This paper derives an analytic expression for the Schwinger pair-production induced current in 1+1D QED with arbitrary time-dependent, spatially inhomogeneous electric fields, using a hybrid bosonization technique that expands in the fermion mass up to order m^2. The authors also confirm the result via adiabatic regularization in the homogeneous case, providing a non-trivial check of the boson-fermion duality.

papers.title: Gravity as Large Scale Structure: Families of CFTs and the Higher-Spin Gap
papers.abstract: We observe an apparently universal behavior in large $N$ conformal field theory (CFT) in $d\geq 2$ dimensions: the single-trace, higher-spin gap obeys the parametric bound $\Delta_{\rm gap} \lesssim (\delta c)^{1/d}$, where $\delta c$ is the central charge increment between successive theories. The origin of this bound is explained heuristically, using a generalized notion of branes that interpolate between conformal points in theory space. Seeking a more precise framework for this picture leads to the central concept of families of CFTs, which tacitly underlies various features and puzzles of AdS/CFT. We develop a working definition of families, with inspiration from families of $L$-functions in number theory, and formulate a family-level version of the gap bound. Interpreted holographically for families of AdS$_{d+1}$ vacua, this bound, when applicable, rules out Planckian scale separation, constrains the size and number of extra dimensions, and explains simple scaling patterns in string/M-theory. It also accounts for why all known large $N$ vector models have a bounded gap.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a universal parametric bound on the higher‑spin gap in large‑N CFTs, linking it to the central‑charge step between neighboring theories via a generalized brane interpolation picture. It then translates this bound into holographic language, showing that families of AdS vacua cannot exhibit Planck‑scale separation and constraining the geometry of extra dimensions, while also explaining why known vector models have bounded gaps.

papers.title: Strong generation of the chiral algebra of $\mathcal N=4$~$SU(N)$ super Yang--Mills theory
papers.abstract: The Schur sector of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory contains infinitely many protected operators, while the invariant polynomials of a single adjoint scalar are organized by finitely many Casimir degrees. I prove that the small $\mathcal N=4$ short multiplets built from these invariants strongly generate the associated chiral algebra, thereby establishing the $SU(N)$ case of the strong-generation conjecture of Beem et al. For every $N\ge2$, all field components associated with degrees $2,\ldots,N$ suffice, in every conformal weight and every degree of the standard relative quantum BRST cohomology. The proof brings together cyclic trace cohomology, quantum lifting, and an arbitrary-degree quartic--odd transport identity. Exact field relations and a finite-rank Newton obstruction exclude every additional lowest space, including non-scalar flavor representations; the required normal-ordering corrections and BRST primitives are derived explicitly. The resulting completeness theorem explains how a finite family of supersymmetric multiplets organizes an unbounded quantum spectrum. Every Schur class is a normal polynomial in their components and derivatives, even when its gauge-theory representative involves fermions and arbitrarily many derivatives. This supplies a uniform set of local inputs for meromorphic operator products, bounds protected state multiplicities before cancellations in an index, and gives an algebraic account of the finite-rank reorganization of protected trace operators.
papers.summary: This work proves that the finite set of small N=4 short multiplets built from invariant polynomials of an adjoint scalar strongly generate the full chiral algebra of SU(N) N=4 SYM, establishing the strong‑generation conjecture for all N≥2. The proof uses cyclic trace cohomology, quantum lifting, and a quartic‑odd transport identity, yielding explicit normal‑ordering corrections and a completeness theorem that organizes the infinite Schur spectrum into a finite set of supersymmetric multiplets.

papers.title: Holomorphic extremal surfaces for pseudoentropy in dS/CFT
papers.authors: Giorgos Anastasiou, Ignacio J. Araya, Avijit Das, Javier Moreno
papers.abstract: We formulate the extremization problem for codimension-two hypersurfaces in de Sitter space in holomorphic coordinates, with real anchoring conditions at future infinity. The resulting equation ($K^I=0$) describes complex bulk realizations extending the usual piecewise Hartle--Hawking construction. We compute holographic pseudoentropy for harmonic deformations of spherical regions of arbitrary size and dimension, confirming its universal expansion through second order in the deformation parameter. The result is independent of the integration contour within each homology class on the complexified extremal surface. Inequivalent classes, labeled by an integer associated with a discrete global-coordinate isometry, differ by a sign of the universal term in odd boundary dimensions and by real finite shifts in even dimensions. For conical defects in dS$_3$ parametrized by a Schwarzschild-dS mass, we also verify the first law of pseudoentropy and the persistence of contour degeneracy within each homology class.
papers.summary: The paper develops a holomorphic formulation of codimension‑two extremal surfaces in de Sitter space, extending Hartle–Hawking constructions to complex geometries, and uses these to compute holographic pseudoentropy for deformed spherical regions, finding universal second‑order behavior independent of contour choice within homology classes. It also verifies the pseudoentropy first law for conical defects in dS$_3$ and shows how different homology classes affect the universal term in odd and even boundary dimensions.

papers.title: Bootstrapping Fermionic Veneziano Amplitudes from Regge Zeros
papers.abstract: We extend the Regge-zero bootstrap of the Veneziano amplitude to tree-level scattering with external fermions. We consider the colour-ordered four-point amplitude of a massless scalar and a massless spin-$\frac12$ fermion, in which fermionic resonances appear in the $s$-channel and bosonic resonances in the $t$-channel. Factoring out a spinor structure that carries the little-group weight of the amplitude, we bootstrap the resulting reduced amplitude, whose residues in each channel vanish at Regge zeros controlled by the trajectory of the opposite channel. Assuming ultrasoft Regge behaviour and that the residues have no zeros other than Regge zeros, we show that both Regge trajectories are linear and that the maximal spins grow with the level as $J_F=n+\frac12$ and $J_B=m+1$. Duality between the fermionic- and bosonic-pole expansions then fixes the reduced amplitude to a Beta function, up to its normalisation and the ratio of the two Regge slopes. Requiring the fermionic and bosonic spectra to be degenerate equates the slopes, and the resulting amplitude coincides with the open superstring amplitude.
papers.summary: The authors extend the Regge-zero bootstrap of the Veneziano amplitude to include external fermions, deriving linear Regge trajectories for both fermionic and bosonic resonances. By imposing duality and degeneracy of spectra, they recover the open superstring amplitude up to normalization.

papers.title: Complex spinodals and supercritical crossovers in Kerr-Newman-AdS$_4$ black holes
papers.authors: Bum-Hoon Lee, Hocheol Lee, Somyadip Thakur
papers.abstract: We study supercritical crossovers in four-dimensional Kerr-Newman-AdS black holes at fixed angular momentum and charge. From the exact enthalpy, we prove uniqueness of the physical critical point and positivity of the quartic Landau coefficient throughout the charge-rotation family, treating the uncharged Kerr-AdS endpoint in separate scaling variables. An exact quartic reduction determines the coexistence entropies and latent heat throughout the subcritical regime. Above criticality, the two physical spinodals continue as a complex conjugate pair. Their real temperature projection defines a Widom-type line, and varying the charge-rotation ratio assembles these lines into a crossover surface. The Landau cusp fixes the imaginary entropy and temperature to scale with the square root and three-halves powers of the pressure displacement from criticality. The projected fold and the local heat capacity ridge share a critical tangent. We derive their leading quadratic temperature separation and prove that the ridge lies at a higher temperature near criticality. Exact endpoint solutions and numerical continuation check these predictions. The cusp exponents are common to the family, while the crossover temperature depends on the thermodynamic criterion used to define it.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes the supercritical phase structure of Kerr-Newman-AdS$_4$ black holes, proving uniqueness of the critical point and deriving exact quartic Landau coefficients. It maps complex spinodals to a Widom-type line and constructs a crossover surface, providing analytic and numerical checks of the critical behavior.

papers.title: The Anyon Atlas
papers.authors: Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham
papers.abstract: We classify possible topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions with up to 22 anyons in the bosonic case and up to 26 in the fermionic case, through the modular data of modular and supermodular tensor categories. We construct such data via congruence representations of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ using a numerical optimization algorithm that scales to high rank. We chart the relations between the resulting theories, including anyon condensations and Chern-Simons realizations. We find examples of modular data that do not appear to arise from any Chern-Simons theory by any sequence of condensations of anyons or gaugings of ordinary global symmetries. These examples give qualitatively new topological quantum field theories, which go beyond any notion of gauge theory. For examples in this class with 11 and 12 anyon types, we solve the pentagon and hexagon equations explicitly, showing that these modular data are realized by full unitary topological quantum field theories. We also introduce https://www.AnyonAtlas.org, an online resource for exploring the data.
papers.summary: This paper classifies modular and supermodular tensor categories up to 22/26 anyons, constructing modular data via congruence representations of SL(2,ℤ) and solving pentagon/hexagon equations for 11–12 anyon cases. It introduces an online atlas and identifies new TQFTs not realizable by Chern‑Simons or symmetry gauging, expanding the landscape of topological phases.

papers.title: Remarks on the Parameter Dependence of QCD$_{2A}$
papers.abstract: Recently it was shown that there are only a few operators that contribute to the (very weak) $N_c$ dependence of the spectrum of two-dimensional adjoint QCD. We provide numerical evidence that none of these operators is dominant. In other words, all operators are necessary to guarantee the faithful representation of the Hamiltonian, resulting in, for instance, exact degeneracies of certain multi-particle state masses.   We provide a complete list of interactions between single- and multi-trace states, which differ by trace-number block, as expected from the Kutasov-Schwimmer universality. The completed list allows for a targeted deformation of the theory to render some masses $N_c$-invariant. Nonetheless, we argue that a small amount of $N_c$ dependence of the theory is unavoidable.   We also investigate the large constituent mass regime $m^2/g^2_{\rm YM}N_c\gg 1$ of the theory at large $N_c$ in the eLCQ approach. We find, among other things, that as the constituent mass grows, eigenstates get purer in parton number, in line with expectations.
papers.summary: This study examines the weak $N_c$ dependence of the spectrum in two-dimensional adjoint QCD, showing that all identified operators are required to preserve exact degeneracies among multi-particle states. Numerical analysis in the eLCQ framework reveals that increasing constituent mass leads to purer parton-number eigenstates, consistent with large-$N_c$ expectations.

papers.title: Non-Riemannian Holography: Long Strings and Soft Hair
papers.authors: Shaun D. Hampton, Hyun-Cheol Kim, Jae-Hyuk Oh, Jeong-Hyuck Park
papers.abstract: We propose an $\mathbf{O}(D,D)$-covariant holographic dictionary for two bulk completions of the Gomis--Ooguri boundary data: Riemannian $AdS_3$ supported by pure NS--NS flux and an everywhere non-Riemannian string Newton--Cartan geometry. An $\mathbf{O}(D,D)$-covariant Codazzi identity yields the boundary conservation law. Both branches share diagonal generalized-metric one-point functions, but only the non-Riemannian branch carries independent normalizable soft hair that couples to long strings without contributing to surface charges or the renormalized on-shell action. Supersymmetric non-Riemannian saddles admit arbitrary chiral Killing-spinor profiles, realizing "supersupersymmetry."
papers.summary: The authors construct an O(D,D)-covariant holographic dictionary for two bulk completions of Gomis–Ooguri boundary data: a Riemannian AdS3 with NS–NS flux and a non‑Riemannian string Newton–Cartan geometry. While both branches share the same diagonal generalized‑metric one‑point functions, only the non‑Riemannian branch supports independent normalizable soft hair that couples to long strings without affecting surface charges or the renormalized on‑shell action, and supersymmetric saddles admit arbitrary chiral Killing‑spinor profiles.

papers.title: Subsystem quantum R\'enyi-Bhattacharyya distance in 2D CFTs and its holographic applications
papers.abstract: We develop a systematic method to compute the subsystem fidelity and R\'enyi fidelity in two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) from the operator product expansion of twist operators, and apply it to the subsystem quantum Bhattacharyya distance (BD) and R\'enyi-Bhattacharyya distance (RBD). We validate the method against exact results in the free massless fermion and boson theories, and then use it to compute the BD and RBD in holographic CFTs between two heavy primary states, between two thermal states, and between a heavy primary state and a thermal state. When the two states differ in their classical, order-$c$ data, the distances are of order $c$, and the states are distinguishable already at the level of classical gravity; when the leading data coincide, the distances are of order $1/c$ at every order of the short interval expansion, so that the distinguishability becomes a perturbative quantum gravity effect. For a heavy primary state and its thermal counterpart, the leading contribution to the BD appears at order $\ell^8$ and is of order $c^0$, whereas the RBD is generically of order $c$, in line with the earlier finding that a heavy primary state and a thermal state share the same order-$c$ entanglement entropy but have different order-$c$ R\'enyi entropies in the short interval expansion.
papers.summary: The authors develop a systematic OPE-based method to compute subsystem fidelity and R'enyi fidelity in 2D CFTs, applying it to the Bhattacharyya distance and its R'enyi generalization. They validate the method against free theories and use it to study holographic CFTs, showing that distinguishability between heavy primary and thermal states is a perturbative quantum gravity effect, with distances scaling as c^0 or c depending on the order‑c data.

papers.title: The long-range Ising CFT: perturbative and nonperturbative approaches
papers.abstract: The long-range Ising model is the prototype of criticality with power-law interactions. In each dimension its interacting critical points form a one-parameter family of nonlocal conformal field theories, weakly coupled at both ends but not in between. We study this family in one, two and three dimensions from several independent directions. We extend the expansion about the generalized free field from three to eight loops and expand about the short-range end. We show that Hamiltonian truncation applies to this nonlocal theory once a truncation artifact is corrected. Where they can be compared, the resummed expansions, Hamiltonian truncation, the numerical renormalization group and Monte Carlo simulations agree on the dimension of the leading $\mathbb{Z}_2$-even scalar at the sub-percent level, as universality requires.
papers.summary: The paper develops high-order perturbative expansions and Hamiltonian truncation techniques for the long-range Ising CFT across 1–3 dimensions, achieving sub-percent agreement with numerical methods on the leading scalar dimension. It demonstrates that nonlocal critical points can be treated with standard CFT tools, providing a benchmark for nonperturbative studies of power-law interacting systems.

papers.title: Higher-Dimensional Test of the Holographic Dual of Entanglement Cohomology
papers.abstract: We extend the holographic test of entanglement cohomology from $d=2$ to higher-dimensional conformal field theories. For a $d$-dimensional CFT with a spherical entangling region $A$, the vacuum modular Hamiltonian is known explicitly, and the boundary relative entropy of a primary-operator perturbation can be computed via conformal Ward identities. On the bulk side, the perturbation is dual to a scalar field in AdS$_{d+1}$, and the bulk canonical energy is computed using the JLMS relation. We carry out the computation explicitly for $d=3$ and $d=4$ and find that the boundary and bulk results agree at first order in the perturbation, with identical coefficients $\kappa_d \Delta^2 / C_T$, where $\kappa_3 = \pi^2/12$ and $\kappa_4 = 3\pi^3/16$. The result extends the quantitative verification of the holographic dual of entanglement cohomology beyond the $d=2$ case treated in the companion paper and confirms that the modular Hamiltonian perturbation is the correct holographic image of the first entanglement cohomology class. We discuss the role of the conformal anomaly, the shape of the entanglement wedge, and an outlook on TsT-deformed backgrounds. \keywords{Entanglement entropy \and Cyclic cohomology \and von Neumann   algebras \and Holography \and Modular Hamiltonian}
papers.summary: This paper extends the holographic test of entanglement cohomology to higher-dimensional CFTs, explicitly computing the boundary relative entropy for primary perturbations and matching it with bulk canonical energy in AdS_{d+1} for d=3,4. The agreement confirms the JLMS relation and supports the conjecture that the modular Hamiltonian perturbation encodes the first entanglement cohomology class in higher dimensions.

papers.title: One-loop unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model from Berends-Giele currents
papers.abstract: We study unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model. We extend tree-level amplitude relations expressed through differential operators to off-shell multiparticle currents and obtain one-loop integrand relations by sewing two off-shell legs. This off-shell approach may also apply to higher-loop integrands.
papers.summary: The authors extend tree-level amplitude relations between Yang–Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model to off-shell Berends–Giele currents, and then sew two legs to produce one-loop integrand identities. This off-shell framework could be generalized to higher-loop integrands, offering a new perspective on the algebraic structure underlying gauge and sigma-model amplitudes.

papers.title: Hubble Susceptibility: Beyond Effective-Mass Spectroscopy in the Cosmological Collider
papers.abstract: In this note, we introduce the Hubble susceptibility of cosmological-collider masses, encoded in the scale dependence of the squeezed-limit oscillation. Heavy fields generically receive Hubble-induced mass corrections during inflation, and we show that the local oscillation frequency and its drift can disentangle such corrections from an intrinsic mass contribution at leading slow-roll and adiabatic order.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a new observable—the Hubble susceptibility—that captures how the effective mass of heavy fields during inflation drifts with the Hubble rate, using the scale dependence of squeezed-limit oscillations to separate intrinsic mass from Hubble-induced corrections. It provides a leading-order slow-roll framework for disentangling these effects in cosmological collider signatures.

papers.title: Millicharged particles and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
papers.abstract: We use geometry to solve a problem in arithmetic relevant for physics. Namely, for any $m$ we find all integer solutions to the equations $\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k = \sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k$, where $k \in \{1,2,3\}$; this seems to be new for $m \geq 5$.   In physics, these are the anomaly cancellation conditions for models with $m$ fermions which can be naturally light and carry small electric charges (a.k.a. millicharged or minicharged particles). The small charges arise by kinetic mixing of the Standard Model $U(1)$ gauge symmetry with an unbroken non-chiral (a.k.a. vector-like) $U(1)$ and the masses are suppressed by a spontaneously-broken chiral $U(1)$.
papers.summary: The paper solves the degree‑3 Prouhet‑Tarry‑Escott problem for arbitrary m, providing all integer solutions to equal sums of first, second, and third powers. These solutions correspond to anomaly‑cancellation conditions in models with m light fermions carrying tiny electric charges, relevant for millicharged particle phenomenology.

papers.title: Quantum Noise from Massive Lorentz--Violating Gravitons: Interferometer Signatures in Very Special Linear Gravity
papers.authors: Jorge Alfaro, Alex Soto, Alessandro Santoni
papers.abstract: In this work we analyse under the Very Special Linear Gravity framework, which introduces a gauge invariant massive graviton with two polarizations, possible signatures of gravitons in a classical gravitational detector. Following the Vernon approach we found dissipative terms consistent with other works and extra terms of order of the graviton mass squared. The model also presents a characteristic feature when a squeezed state is considered. In such case, a contribution that distinguishes the sign of the squeezing phase is present.
papers.summary: This paper studies a Very Special Linear Gravity model that yields a gauge‑invariant massive graviton with two polarizations and predicts dissipative and mass‑dependent corrections to interferometer signals, including a distinctive phase‑dependent effect when the graviton is in a squeezed state. The analysis employs a Vernon‑type approach to derive these signatures and highlights potential experimental observables for classical gravitational detectors.

papers.title: Quantum Relaxation Dynamics of Vacuum Energy from Pre-Geometric Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate a quantum relaxation mechanism for the vacuum energy density arising from the spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) $SO(1,4)\to SO(1,3)$, driven by a Higgs field $\Phi$ in a MacDowell--Mansouri pre-geometric gravity framework. The theory predicts a countably infinite set of vacua, corresponding to distinct topological sectors, for a periodic Higgs potential with intervening barriers. This structure gives rise to a series of dualities and see-saw relations connecting fundamental scales---the Planck mass and the Cosmological Constant---to topological parameters such as the Gauss-Bonnet coupling and the $\theta$-term, all of which emerge only after SSB. A striking consequence is the quantization of the vacuum energy into discrete levels. Starting from a vacuum expectation value $\langle \Phi\rangle = v_1$ associated with a large vacuum energy, the system evolves via quantum tunneling through the infinite landscape of minima. Crucially, we demonstrate that the transition probability is maximized for the ordered sequence $ \Lambda_1 > \cdots > \Lambda_k > \cdots$, where the Cosmological Constant decreases monotonically toward the asymptotic attractor $\Lambda_\infty = 0$.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a pre‑geometric gravity model where spontaneous symmetry breaking of SO(1,4) to SO(1,3) yields a Higgs field that generates a periodic potential with infinitely many topological vacua, leading to a discrete spectrum of vacuum energies. The authors show that quantum tunneling between these vacua drives the cosmological constant to zero, offering a novel relaxation mechanism for the vacuum energy.

papers.title: Boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in holography
papers.authors: Yu Shi, Xinwu Liu, Liping Li, Chikun Ding, Yuebing Zhou, Changqing Liu, Sheng Long
papers.abstract: Finite boundary drives ending at the same charge density can select different relaxation channels. We demonstrate this in a probe Abelian--Higgs model on a fixed AdS black brane with a stable normal endpoint. Charge exchange during preparation modifies scalar propagation and source coupling. Density history and radial Maxwell feedback during and after the drive leave a cubic slow amplitude even after linear slow-mode cancellation. For the tested protocols at $\rho_f=3$, the density-history term interferes constructively with the net radial feedback; its modulus is 85--89\% of that of the total cubic coefficient. Calculated from the low-order equations alone, this total coefficient predicts the compensating pulse. Full nonlinear evolution confirms the reduction from $O(\epsilon^3)$ to $O(\epsilon^5)$ in the source amplitude $\epsilon$, with approximately 600-fold suppression for the representative protocol at $\epsilon=0.05$. Compensation extends the window of fast-channel relaxation without changing the final quasinormal-mode spectrum; early distance crossing already arises from linear interference. Fully tuned two- and three-pulse preparations suppress one and two slow modes, respectively, within numerical resolution. Local analysis establishes finite-pulse reachability of strong Mpemba states with vanishing selected asymptotic slow-mode coefficients. Charge-neutral controls retain a total-time advantage from a common input when the full subsequent control duration is included.
papers.summary: The paper studies how boundary driving protocols in a probe Abelian–Higgs model on an AdS black brane can selectively suppress slow relaxation modes, achieving Mpemba-like fast equilibration without altering the final quasinormal spectrum. By tuning multi-pulse drives, the authors demonstrate a dramatic reduction of cubic nonlinearities, effectively extending the window of rapid relaxation in holographic systems.

papers.title: Dispersion of three-dimensional oscillons: a standing-wave perspective
papers.authors: I. V. Barashenkov, R. De Sousa, N. V. Alexeeva, A. Dika, E. V. Zemlyanaya
papers.abstract: A spherically symmetric standing wave confined within a finite-radius ball, with weak radiative exchange between its core and boundary, provides a model for an intermediate stage in the adiabatic evolution of the $\phi^4$ oscillon. We employ a multiscale variational framework to derive an approximate description of these standing waves and their energy-frequency relation. The resulting dispersion curve is compared with that obtained from numerical solutions of the boundary value problem for the $\phi^4$ equation on a two dimensional (time and radius) domain. The agreement between the numerical and variational results is excellent near the endpoint of the continuous spectrum but deteriorates as $\omega$ is reduced below $0.85 \omega_0$. We attribute this discrepancy to the growth of the radiation wing, which is neglected in the variational ansatz.
papers.summary: This work studies spherically symmetric standing-wave solutions (oscillons) in the φ^4 theory, deriving an approximate dispersion relation via a multiscale variational approach and comparing it to numerical solutions. The agreement is good near the spectrum endpoint but worsens at lower frequencies due to neglected radiation.

papers.title: U(1) Current Diffusion in Gauss-Bonnet Holography
papers.authors: A. Naveena Kumara, Shreyas Punacha, Kartheek Hegde
papers.abstract: We study holographic $U(1)$ charge transport using a probe Maxwell field in a five-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet-AdS black-brane background. Within the all-order linearised fluid/gravity framework, we derive the off-shell constitutive relation and determine the diffusion function and electric and magnetic conductivities analytically in the hydrodynamic regime and numerically at generic frequency and momentum. To first order in the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, the leading diffusion constant remains unchanged in our normalization, while its frequency dependence and the electric conductivity receive nontrivial corrections. The deformation also generates a nonvanishing leading magnetic conductivity. Beyond the hydrodynamic regime, it modifies the transport profiles while preserving the damped behaviour of the diffusion function. The corresponding memory kernel vanishes at negative times, supporting a retarded constitutive response.
papers.summary: The paper investigates U(1) charge transport in a five‑dimensional Gauss‑Bonnet‑AdS black‑brane using a probe Maxwell field, deriving the full off‑shell constitutive relation and computing diffusion, electric, and magnetic conductivities both analytically in the hydrodynamic limit and numerically at arbitrary frequency and momentum. It finds that the Gauss‑Bonnet coupling leaves the leading diffusion constant unchanged but introduces nontrivial frequency dependence, modifies the electric conductivity, generates a leading magnetic conductivity, and yields a retarded memory kernel that vanishes at negative times.

papers.title: The $A_3$ Narain family over $\mathbb{Z}_4$
papers.abstract: The code $\{000,220,202,022\}\subset\mathbb{Z}_4^3$ realizes the split $A_3$ root-weight gluing construction as ordinary Construction A, preserving the Lorentzian pairing and the positive energy form. For two hyperbolic pairs of $A_3$ blocks, the twenty-two even self-dual gluing codes form seven block-monomial classes. Explicit metric and $B$-field representatives and theta series distinguish exactly seven T-duality classes in this family at central charge six; the one-pair family has two classes at central charge three. For arbitrary $d$, the chiral root system on either side is $A_1^{3m}$, where $m$ counts the words $(2e_i,2e_i)$ in the gluing code. Exactly one two-pair class has no zero-$B$ T-duality frame. Intersections of gluing codes determine finite shift orbifolds between the backgrounds, with the target code specifying the twisted-sector projections.
papers.summary: This work constructs a family of $A_3$ Narain lattices via a $mathbb{Z}_4$ code, classifying the resulting T‑duality orbits and identifying seven distinct backgrounds at central charge six. The authors also analyze the associated theta series and orbifold projections, providing explicit metrics and $B$‑fields for each class.

papers.title: On Integrable Deformations of CFTs and Integrable Two-Dimensional Sigma Models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the systems of screening charges corresponding to $\eta$-deformed $O(N)$ and $OSp(N|2m)$ sigma models. These sigma models can be represented as integrable deformations of certain conformal field theories. Based on the case of $O(N)$ sigma models, which were conjectured in previous works by A.V. Litvinov and co-authors to be an integrable deformation of the conformal field theory corresponding to the algebras $W(D(n+1|n))$ and $W(D(n|n))$ for the cases $N=2n+2$ and $N=2n+1$ at $n \geq 1$, respectively, we formulate a hypothesis on how to write down the system of screening charges for the conformal field theory whose integrable deformation defines the $\eta$-deformed $OSp(N|2m)$ sigma model for the case of odd $N=2n+1$, asymptotically free models with $N-2m-2>0$ and $n \geq 2$, $m \geq 1$. This hypothesis is explicitly verified for the cases of $OSp(5|2)$, $OSp(7|2)$, and $OSp(7|4)$, which were separately investigated in the work of M.N. Alfimov and co-authors.
papers.summary: This work constructs the screening charge systems underlying η‑deformed O(N) and OSp(N|2m) sigma models, showing that these deformations can be viewed as integrable deformations of specific W‑algebra CFTs. The authors verify their hypothesis for several low‑rank examples, thereby extending the dictionary between integrable sigma models and W‑algebra representations.

papers.title: An explicit product for the on-shell higher-spin algebra in $AdS_d$-space
papers.abstract: For $d>3$ we construct the product of the bosonic on-shell higher-spin algebra directly on the AdS-traceless representatives. We find the traceless projector in closed form, determine all linear relations among the trace-producing operators, and prove that every class modulo the $\mathfrak{sp}(2)$ ideal has a unique traceless representative. The resulting product is an explicit differential operator, which we test on the $\mathfrak{so}(d-1,2)$ generators. A toy model shows how the factorisation lifts from bilinear products to trilinear ones in minimal $A_\infty$-algebras.
papers.summary: The authors construct an explicit differential-product for the bosonic on-shell higher-spin algebra in AdS_d (d>3) by deriving a closed-form traceless projector and showing that each equivalence class modulo the sp(2) ideal has a unique traceless representative. They verify the construction against so(d-1,2) generators and illustrate how the factorisation extends to trilinear products in minimal A∞-algebras, offering a concrete tool for higher-spin interactions in AdS/CFT.

papers.title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
papers.authors: Shengyi Guan, Qiang Jia, Jiahua Tian, Yi-Nan Wang
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern--Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux--charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov--Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel--Watts theory.
papers.summary: This paper studies the large‑level limit of doubled Chern–Simons theory, showing that line operators become BF lines with magnetic flux set by the average weight and electric charge given by the difference. It proves that modular transformations of torus states converge to their BF counterparts, and speculates on the boundary 2d theory and interfaces, relating them to known CFTs such as the Runkel–Watts theory.

papers.title: R\'enyi Multi-entropy for Stabilizer States: A Finite Field Gauss Sum Problem
papers.authors: Bartlomiej Czech, Yichen Feng, Jonathan Harper, Xin-Xiang Ju, Yang Zhao
papers.abstract: R\'enyi multi-entropy probes multi-partite structure beyond bipartite spectra, but its behavior in general quantum states and the entanglement structure it captures remain poorly understood. We develop a finite field Gauss sum framework for calculating it in stabilizer states. Within this framework, the replica contraction reduces to a quadratic Gauss sum if and only if the state is locally unitarily equivalent to a stabilizer state. We obtain analytic expressions for the R\'enyi multi-entropy of all tree graph states and large families of loop graph states. In contrast to their flat bipartite R\'enyi spectra, stabilizer states generically have nonflat R\'enyi multi-entropy spectra.
papers.summary: This paper develops a finite‑field Gauss sum framework to compute the R'enyi multi‑entropy for stabilizer states, showing that the replica contraction simplifies to a quadratic Gauss sum only for states locally equivalent to stabilizer states. It provides analytic results for tree and many loop graph states, revealing that stabilizer states generally exhibit nonflat R'enyi multi‑entropy spectra unlike their flat bipartite spectra.

papers.title: Mechanical angular momentum loss at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ from static and radiative gravitons
papers.authors: Lara Bohnenblust, Carl Jordan Eriksen, Gustav Uhre Jakobsen, Kathrin Stoldt, Andrii Yanovets
papers.abstract: We determine the loss of mechanical angular momentum $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$ of two gravitationally scattering bodies at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ using worldline quantum field theory (WQFT). The gravitational memory effect, a phenomenon of the early- and late-time behaviour of the gravitational field, leads to static contributions to $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. We illuminate how these arise: the linear memory contributes through so-called static correlators, while the nonlinear memory vanishes at this order due to symmetry considerations. The computation of the remaining, dynamical part resembles that of the $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ impulse. We generate its integrand using a reformulation of the WQFT Feynman rules that conserves four-momentum at every vertex and plainly exhibits the classical loops. The three-loop integrals are reduced to master integrals, whose differential equations and boundary matching in the post-Newtonian limit we describe in some detail. In contrast to conservative effects at this order, only polylogarithms appear. While individual contributions to the dynamical part are divergent, these cancel in $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. The quadratic-in-radiation part of our result reproduces earlier results, while the complete result agrees with existing post-Newtonian results.
papers.summary: This paper computes the loss of mechanical angular momentum for two-body gravitational scattering at fourth order in Newton's constant using worldline quantum field theory. It identifies static memory contributions and evaluates the dynamical part via three-loop integrals, confirming consistency with post-Newtonian results.

papers.title: Field theory guides Monte Carlo in the one-dimensional long-range Ising model
papers.abstract: The statistical long-range Ising (LRI) model in one dimension provides a family of some of the simplest non-exactly solvable critical points. These critical points are described by long-range conformal field theories (CFTs) that are well understood analytically with perturbative expansions and some exact results. Guided by this, we revisit the Monte Carlo (MC) approach to the corresponding lattice model which has many favorable features compared to other systems studied with MC methods. In particular, with very modest computational cost, we are able to estimate scaling dimensions of leading and subleading operators as well as the associated three-point functions, and even certain four-point functions. These results help highlight the fact that 1d LRI CFTs are a phenomenal playground to more generally test non-perturbative methods and ideas for strongly coupled CFTs.
papers.summary: This paper demonstrates that Monte Carlo simulations of the one-dimensional long-range Ising model can accurately extract scaling dimensions and multi-point correlation functions of the associated long-range CFT, providing a computationally efficient testbed for non-perturbative CFT methods. The authors show that modest computational resources suffice to recover leading and subleading operator dimensions, as well as three- and four-point functions, underscoring the utility of 1D LRI CFTs for benchmarking analytic and numerical approaches.

papers.title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
papers.authors: Alexander Chervov, Ilia Gaiur, Sergey Galkin, Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk, Volodya Rubtsov, Shamil Shakirov
papers.abstract: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.
papers.summary: This work derives new representations for quantum A‑periods of local ${mathbb P}^1	imes{mathbb P}^1$ using TBA equations and continued fractions, providing efficient recursion formulas and quantum corrections to the Picard‑Fuchs equation. It also connects these periods to combinatorial structures such as constant terms of Laurent polynomials and random walks on the Heisenberg group, with speculative remarks on AI applications.

papers.title: Algebraic decomposition and topological fibrations of the $U(4) \to SU(2)$ quotient space
papers.abstract: We investigate the algebraic and topological properties of the unitary group $U(4)$ subjected to a non-standard continuous symmetry breaking cascade down to an $SU(2)_H$ subgroup. By explicitly embedding the unbroken $SU(2)_H$ symmetry into the lower-right quadrant of the fundamental matrix representation, we demonstrate that the resulting 12-dimensional quotient space, $SU(4)/SU(2)_H$, undergoes a strictly asymmetric geometric partition. This specific breaking pattern uniquely isolates an 8-dimensional sector that retains closed commutation relations, forming a rigorous $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ Lie subalgebra. Concurrently, it isolates a 4-dimensional off-diagonal sector that fails to close algebraically, generating a purely non-linear topological coset. By analyzing the global spherical fibrations of the manifold, we show that this non-linear territory reduces to a $\mathbb{C}P^1 \cong S^2$ base space. Consequently, continuous mappings from a 3-dimensional spatial boundary are classified by the third homotopy group, $\pi_3(S^2) \cong \mathbb{Z}$, guaranteeing absolute vacuum stability via the integer-quantized Hopf invariant. Ultimately, this framework demonstrates that a non-simple unitary group can organically provide a mathematically rigorous geometric template capable of simultaneously accommodating both continuous gauge symmetries and stable, non-perturbative topological sectors.
papers.summary: The paper studies the coset space SU(4)/SU(2)_H arising from a non‑standard symmetry breaking pattern of U(4), revealing an 8‑dimensional su(3) subalgebra and a 4‑dimensional non‑linear sector that fibers over CP^1. It shows that maps from a 3‑sphere into this base are classified by π3(S^2)=Z, yielding an integer‑valued Hopf invariant that guarantees vacuum stability.

papers.title: How do late-time photons "record" primordial curvature perturbations?
papers.authors: Tomotaka Kuroda, Fumiya Sano, Yusuke Yamada
papers.abstract: Inflationary cosmology faces a fundamental gap between primordial quantum fluctuations and the classical cosmic history inferred from observations. Although the primordial quantum state is a superposition of field configurations, standard cosmology assumes one definite realization of curvature perturbations and uses classical perturbation theory to describe the resulting gravitational potentials, CMB anisotropies, and large-scale structure. Squeezing and decoherence of primordial fluctuations alone do not explain why this one-realization description is physically meaningful. We address this issue through Cosmological Classical Branches (CCBs), using the quantum-information-theoretic notion of physical records. In CCBs, distinct late-time matter components carry compatible records of the same primordial configuration. A record in one component makes that configuration readable, while a disjoint compatible record suppresses interference accessible to operations on the first. Each branch thus admits a common c-number primordial label at finite resolution, while the global quantum superposition persists. This Letter summarizes the framework developed in Ref.~\cite{Kuroda2026CCB}.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Cosmological Classical Branches (CCBs) as a framework to reconcile the quantum superposition of primordial fluctuations with the single classical realization observed in late-time cosmology, using the concept of physical records carried by distinct matter components. It shows how compatible records suppress interference and allow a common classical label for the primordial configuration while preserving the global quantum superposition.

papers.title: Group averaging and the geometry of physical quantum states: from normalizable solutions to solvable loop quantum cosmology
papers.abstract: In canonical quantum gravity the physical states solve the constraints but are typically not normalizable in the kinematical Hilbert space. Group averaging constructs them from normalizable kinematical seeds. We describe the geometry of this seed-to-state map in the language of geometric quantum mechanics.   When averaging is an orthogonal projection, the admissible kinematical rays form a holomorphic vector bundle over the physical ray space. The embedded exact solutions form its zero section, and its fibers are strictly larger than gauge orbits. Observables descend to the base exactly when the Hessian of the squared constraint vanishes along their flow.   For distributional physical states, group averaging on an explicit Sobolev test space yields an affine bundle of representatives. Its sections are embeddings of the physical ray space whose images contain no exact solutions. The test-space inner product singles out one of them, and narrowing the seed profile gives Weyl sequences of approximate solutions.   We apply this to solvable loop quantum cosmology. Group averaging reproduces the Klein--Gordon physical inner product on an explicit test space. Because the scalar-field momentum enters the constraint quadratically, the constraint spectrum has an edge near the shell. The canonical section is then mode-dependent and not K\"ahler isometric, and the canonical seeds of small universes are biased off the shell. The edge also separates the Page--Wootters state from the slice of the Klein--Gordon solution. An ideal clock shows none of these effects.   The results separate the canonical structures, namely physical rays, physical geometry and Dirac observables, from those that depend on a choice of seeds, test space or clock.
papers.summary: This paper studies the geometric structure of group averaging in canonical quantum gravity, showing how kinematical seeds map to physical states via holomorphic vector bundles and affine bundles, and applies the formalism to solvable loop quantum cosmology to recover the Klein–Gordon inner product and analyze the role of the scalar field momentum. It highlights how the choice of seeds, test space, or clock affects the canonical structure and physical observables, providing insights into the geometry of physical quantum states.

papers.title: Multimessenger Probes of Primordial Black Holes with Gravitational Wave and 21 cm Observations
papers.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from the collapse of curvature perturbations in the early universe are known to have an associated gravitational wave signal sourced by the same scalar perturbations. In this work, we show that there is a complementarity between these gravitational waves and modifications of the 21 cm global signal during the cosmic dark ages due to PBH evaporation. For PBHs in the range $ M_{\rm PBH} \sim 5 \times 10^{13} \, {\rm g} - 10^{17} \, {\rm g}$, there is a correlated signal in gravitational waves in the LISA, deci-Hz, and ground based regimes from $f_{\rm GW} \sim 10^{-3} \, {\rm Hz} - 20 \, {\rm Hz}$ and in the 21 cm global signal from $z \sim 300 - 30$. These observations are entirely independent of each other and within the reach of near-future experiments, making a combined measurement a novel multimessenger probe of primordial physics.
papers.summary: This paper investigates the joint signatures of primordial black holes in gravitational wave spectra and 21 cm cosmology, focusing on PBHs with masses 5×10¹³–10¹⁷ g. It shows that LISA, deci‑Hz, and ground‑based detectors can probe the same mass range that affects the cosmic dark‑age 21 cm signal, offering a multimessenger test of early‑universe physics.

papers.title: Electric Flux as a Criterion for String Breaking and Schwinger Pair Production
papers.abstract: We define string breaking by the midpoint electric field falling to half a flux unit. In the massive Schwinger model, an energy balance between intact string and screened configuration predicts this separation using only vacuum observables and meson masses as input. We observe numerically that this half flux point corresponds to equal weights of the two configurations thus explaining the observed peak of the entanglement entropy as maximal uncertainty of the binary flux. The same binary uncertainty explains the entanglement peak at the vacuum transition. Near breaking, screening organizes part of the spatial entanglement between the string interior and exterior into a nearly maximally entangled bit. Within the selected flux sectors, this approximate encoded Bell pair records whether the flux is screened and nearly separates from the remaining correlations. The vacuum transition exhibits the same structure. The string and the $\theta$-vacuum reveal a matching structure of the capacity of entanglement minimum at their transition point, linking their entanglement spectra. The transition rearranges degrees of freedom coherently as revealed by the entanglement asymmetry and Robustness of Magic of disjoint subregions. Finally, we construct the $\theta$-vacuum and string wavefunctions with high fidelity using a restricted Boltzmann machine ansatz.
papers.summary: The authors propose a criterion for string breaking in the massive Schwinger model based on the midpoint electric field dropping to half a flux unit, showing that this point coincides with equal weights of intact and screened configurations and explains the peak in entanglement entropy. They further analyze the entanglement structure near the transition, revealing a nearly maximally entangled bit that records screening, and construct the corresponding wavefunctions using a restricted Boltzmann machine.

papers.title: Analytic quantum invariants
papers.authors: Rinat Kashaev, Vladimir Mangazeev, Marcos Marino
papers.abstract: Using a deformed Borel-Laplace resummation, we propose a framework for repackaging quantum invariants as analytic invariants. We illustrate our approach through a detailed analysis of the coloured Jones polynomials of several simple knots, deriving explicit expressions for the resulting analytic invariants in terms of $(q,X)$-series. These invariants are closely related to, but generally distinct from, those obtained via the conventional Borel resummation of the Melvin-Morton-Rozansky expansion. As a further example, we construct an analytic invariant from a sequence of two-variable polynomials conjectured to be the Links-Gould polynomials of the figure-eight knot, associated with the quantum superalgebras $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}(n|1))$. Finally, we apply our technique to $q$-series arising in the study of three-manifold invariants, revealing connections with mock modular forms.
papers.summary: The authors develop a deformed Borel–Laplace resummation framework that rewrites quantum knot invariants, such as colored Jones and Links‑Gould polynomials, as analytic $(q,X)$‑series. Their method uncovers new connections between these series and mock modular forms, hinting at deeper links to number‑theoretic structures like L‑functions and Langlands duality.

papers.title: Linearised gravitational radiation in de Sitter spacetime at all multipole orders
papers.abstract: We derive the linearised gravitational waves generated by a localised matter source in the Poincare patch of de Sitter spacetime at arbitrary multipole order. The linearised de Sitter problem is mapped exactly to an auxiliary flat-space problem in harmonic gauge, with a conserved source built from the physical stress tensor. This allows us to use the multipole expansion of Damour and Iyer verbatim, and yields the exterior metric at all orders in terms of two families of radiative multipole moments given as explicit integrals of the physical stress tensor. The de Sitter tail is absorbed entirely into the auxiliary stress tensor, so that neither the moments nor the canonical exterior metric carry an integral over the past history of the source. As a check, we recover the known quadrupolar metric: in the quadrupolar truncation it is our canonical field up to a residual gauge transformation, which we construct explicitly.
papers.summary: This work derives the full multipole expansion of linearized gravitational waves in the Poincaré patch of de Sitter space by mapping the problem to a flat-space harmonic-gauge calculation, yielding explicit expressions for radiative multipole moments in terms of the stress tensor. The authors recover the known quadrupole result and show that the de Sitter tail is absorbed into the auxiliary source, simplifying the exterior metric.

papers.title: Grey-body factors of black holes
papers.abstract: Grey-body factors describe the frequency-dependent transmission of fields through the effective potential generated by a black hole or another compact object. They convert the idealized thermal spectrum of Hawking radiation into the spectrum measured by an observer, determine absorption and scattering cross sections, and provide real-frequency observables complementary to quasinormal modes. In this review, we present a unified account of grey-body factors in black-hole physics and related systems. We formulate the scattering problem for asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter spacetimes, and discuss the connections between transmission coefficients, absorption cross sections, Hawking radiation, and ringdown. We also review methods for their computation and survey recent developments, including the correspondence between grey-body factors and quasinormal modes, their stability under deformations of the effective potential, wormhole transmission and superradiance, and their behavior in modified theories of gravity. Finally, we discuss the appearance of grey-body factors in gauge/gravity duality, where absorption probabilities in the bulk are related to correlation functions and transport coefficients in the boundary theory.
papers.summary: This review surveys how grey‑body factors modify Hawking radiation spectra, link absorption cross sections to quasinormal modes, and extend to asymptotically flat, dS, and AdS spacetimes, including gauge/gravity duality applications.

papers.title: Complexification of the Kerr-AdS black hole thermodynamic phase transition
papers.authors: Fei Guo, Zhen-Ming Xu, Robert B. Mann
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a systematic complex-analytical framework for investigating the thermodynamics of high-dimensional singly spinning Kerr-AdS black holes. By performing an analytical continuation of the black hole horizon radius into the complex plane, we map the thermodynamic behavior for the black hole to the zeros distribution of the corresponding analytical function. In the region below the critical point, this approach provides the criterion for identifying phase transitions and reveals that the zeroth-order phase transition does not alter the underlying thermodynamic topological structure of the black hole. In the supercritical region, based on the Lee-Yang theory of phase transition, we construct the Widom line to characterize the supercritical crossover behavior for the Kerr-AdS black holes. This study provides a new perspective on the thermodynamic analysis of black holes.
papers.summary: This work develops a complex-analytic method to study the thermodynamics of high-dimensional singly spinning Kerr-AdS black holes by analytically continuing the horizon radius. It uses Lee–Yang zeros to identify phase transitions below the critical point and constructs a Widom line to describe supercritical crossover behavior.

papers.title: Where should we look for the deviation from quantum mechanics?
papers.abstract: We argue that the experimental measurement of the lifetime and decay law of metastable helium is a promising way to find a deviation from quantum mechanics. We analyze the decay of the metastable state for a quartic deformation of quantum mechanics. We find that the absolute change of the mean lifetime can be significant even if the modification is small. We show that, in the Wigner--Weisskopf approximation, the deviation from the exponential law in the modified theory can occur on time scales comparable with the lifetime.
papers.summary: The authors propose measuring the lifetime of metastable helium to detect deviations from standard quantum mechanics, focusing on a quartic deformation of the theory. They find that even small modifications can produce significant changes in the mean lifetime and non‑exponential decay behavior on timescales comparable to the lifetime.

papers.title: A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe
papers.abstract: We study a flat three-torus universe whose contraction is turned around by the negative Casimir energy of Standard Model fields. The trace anomaly forbids conformal matter alone to turn an anisotropic universe around, so matter with $w<1/3$, most cheaply a positive potential, must supply the negative trace; with antiperiodic fermions the Standard Model supplies the negative energy, and the universe turns at an edge of 722 reduced Planck lengths. There the Higgs quartic coupling is negative, but zero-point fluctuations of the constant gauge modes confine the Higgs zero mode down to a finite-volume threshold $\lambda_c\approx-0.012$, below the Standard Model value $-0.0098$. The Higgs survives with probability above $1/2$ for a top-quark pole mass below $172.96$ GeV ($\bar m_t<163.16$ GeV; $\alpha_s(M_Z)=0.1180$), and with probability $\approx0.7$ for current data, given a curvature coupling $\xi_H\gtrsim0.08$ at the scale $\bar M_{\mathrm{P}}/722$. The turning point can hold only about five quanta of the lowest modes, whereas a reheating coupling in a time-symmetric past would produce radiation exceeding the Casimir energy by at least $10^{94}$, so we read the turn as a beginning rather than a bounce. Negative Casimir energy cannot hold the shape of the torus: the shape state can be real at most once, and for a real Gaussian state survival of the shape on both branches with $90\%$ probability requires that moment to lie within $0.35$ Hubble times of the turn. The natural state, real at the turn, freezes the torus into a nearly rectangular box whose sides typically differ by $16$-$18\%$. The microwave background can read this fossil only if the shortest cycle lies between $0.985$ and about $1.04$ last-scattering diameters. A top-quark pole mass above $173.7$ GeV, within reach of FCC-ee, would exclude this beginning (Bayes factor $\lesssim0.03$).
papers.summary: The paper studies a flat three‑torus universe whose contraction is reversed by the negative Casimir energy of Standard Model fields, analyzing the Higgs quartic coupling, survival probabilities, and the shape dynamics at the turning point. It concludes that the universe’s beginning is more likely a one‑way turn rather than a bounce, with implications for the allowed top‑quark mass and the torus geometry observable in the CMB.

papers.title: Scalar fields in the background of a linear Vaidya spacetime
papers.abstract: We study, in a semiclassical, quasi-stationary approximation, the entanglement properties of massless scalar fields near the event horizon of a dynamical black hole modeled by an ingoing Vaidya metric with a linearly decaying mass. In the near-horizon limit, the geometry becomes conformally equivalent to an eternal black hole, allowing the use of modular theory to analyze vacuum entanglement.
