We first study the modifications to the entanglement across the bifurcation surface of such a black hole from that of an eternal one. The conformal factor accounting for the evaporation modifies the Bogoliubov transformation, inducing a phase in the thermofield-double-like structure of the global vacuum. This phase change of the vacuum state is a consequence of the adiabatic shift of the horizon. A quantitative measure of the entanglement change due to the phase is obtained through the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. We compare the CHSH inequalities in the vacuum states for the static and the linear Vaidya black holes and find that the CHSH correlation quantity for the latter is decreased by a factor depending on the evaporation rate.   Next, we discuss the changes that must be considered for the linear Vaidya black hole formed from gravitational collapse. For this purpose we adapt an analysis by Wald for the case of the Schwarzschild black hole. We find, as expected, the near-horizon structure and state do not approach that of the eternal black hole. Rather, the thermal factor is modified by a factor incorporating the change in the black hole mass due to evaporation. The entangled global vacuum state again has a thermofield double structure with the modification mentioned above.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes how a linearly decaying Vaidya black hole modifies the vacuum entanglement structure compared to an eternal black hole, using modular theory and a phase shift in the thermofield-double-like vacuum. It quantifies the reduction in CHSH correlations due to evaporation and discusses the differences for a collapse-formed Vaidya black hole.

papers.title: Negative-Definite Plumbings and New Unknotting Numbers
papers.abstract: We use Neumann's normal form to decide whether the double branched cover of a knot bounds a negative-definite plumbing tree in either orientation, starting from the recognised Seifert or graph-manifold structure of the cover. For many non-alternating knots with at most thirteen crossings whose unknotting numbers were unknown, this identifies the cases in which the Heegaard Floer homology of the cover can be computed from such a plumbing, and shows for most of the others that it cannot. We determine 112 new unknotting numbers. For 43 of them, the lower bound rests on Heegaard Floer homology computed from the plumbing; for the other 69, it comes from linking pairings and from a theorem of McCoy and Park on special alternating knots. Finally, we show that the knot 13n1587 is a further explicit counterexample to the Bernhard--Jablan conjecture, after 13n3370.
papers.summary: This work develops a combinatorial method to decide whether the double branched cover of a knot bounds a negative-definite plumbing tree, allowing the computation of Heegaard Floer homology for many non-alternating knots. By applying this to over a hundred knots, the authors determine new unknotting numbers and provide counterexamples to a longstanding conjecture, offering new data that could inform topological quantum field theory approaches to knot invariants.

papers.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field. However, it was recently shown that this description is incomplete: their inherent gravitational self-interactions can squeeze the field, producing a quantum feature beyond the classical description. Here we analyze squeezing of light dark matter in the presence of decoherence. We show that squeezing is continuously generated, and rapidly enough to survive dissipation, and may also remain present under thermal fluctuations and dephasing. Our results demonstrate that dark matter might possess persistent quantum features and motivate further investigation of their implications for dark matter detection.
papers.summary: The paper studies how gravitational self‑interactions of light axion dark matter generate quantum squeezing, and shows that this squeezing can survive decoherence and thermal effects. It suggests that axion dark matter may retain persistent quantum features that could impact detection strategies.

papers.title: Gravitational Instability of Cold Axion Dark Matter Beyond Minimal Coupling
papers.abstract: Following recent observations of unexpectedly massive galaxies at high redshift by the James Webb Space Telescope, the revision of Dark Matter (DM) models --specifically regarding how DM couples to gravity-- has become a central topic in Cosmology. In this paper, we develop an axion model for Cold Dark Matter (CDM) with a non-minimal coupling to gravity. From this framework, we evaluate the gravitational instability in the hydrodynamic limit. Our results demonstrate how gravitational instabilities depend on the non-minimal coupling parameter, providing a novel tool for aligning with the high-redshift observations from the James Webb Space Telescope.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a cold axion dark matter model with a non‑minimal coupling to gravity and studies its hydrodynamic gravitational instability. The analysis shows that the instability growth rate depends on the coupling strength, offering a potential explanation for the unexpectedly massive high‑redshift galaxies observed by JWST.

papers.title: Interferometric trilemma for ultraviolet-softened gravity
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet-softened extensions of general relativity can weaken gravity at short distances, whereas a positive K\"all\'en--Lehmann spectral density forbids gravity from falling below Newtonian strength. Which property of the mediator must such a weakening sacrifice? For Lorentz-invariant Gaussian mediators coupled linearly to the conserved stress tensor, we formulate three independent interferometric conditions that jointly imply this bound: visibility is never amplified, decoherence is fixed by the energy radiated by the difference source, and no interferometer responds to a later one. At tree level, the three ghost prescriptions of quadratic gravity each violate exactly one: negative-norm ghosts amplify coherence, negative-energy ghosts decohere without positive energy transfer from the difference source, and a time-symmetric fakeon response produces advanced fringe shifts. Any universal short-distance weakening of gravity therefore certifies that its mediator violates one of these conditions, and the observables proposed to certify quantum gravity become consistency tests of its ultraviolet completion.
papers.summary: The paper investigates how ultraviolet-softened gravity models can weaken short-distance gravitational interactions while respecting a positive Källén–Lehmann spectral density. It establishes three interferometric criteria—visibility, decoherence, and causal response—that any such weakening must violate, providing a framework to test quantum gravity consistency via interferometry.

papers.title: The Geometry of the "Gauge Argument"
papers.authors: James Owen Weatherall, Benjamin H. Feintzeig
papers.abstract: We show how the "gauge argument", widely criticized by philosophers as ad hoc and unconvincing, may be reconstructed rigorously, and, we believe, convincingly, as an argument concerning the geometry of vector bundles. In this form, the gauge argument has two parts, the first of which is strongly analogous to the Weyl-Stein argument for Galilean spacetime as the appropriate setting for Newtonian gravitation; and the second of which invokes a classic result in the Yang-Mills theory literature, due to Utiyama [1956, "Invariant Theoretical Interpretation of Interaction", Phys. Rev. 101, 1597].
papers.summary: The paper reconstructs the gauge argument as a rigorous geometric argument about vector bundles, paralleling the Weyl–Stein argument for Galilean spacetime and invoking Utiyama’s theorem in Yang–Mills theory. It clarifies the role of gauge symmetry in field theory but does not directly address holography, celestial amplitudes, or other listed interests.

papers.title: Black hole free energy landscapes from constrained instantons
papers.authors: Shan-Ping Wu, Jia-Zhou Liu, Yu-Xiao Liu, Shao-Wen Wei
papers.abstract: We apply gravitational path integral factorization to provide a semiclassical interpretation of generalized black hole free energy landscapes at fixed external temperature and angular velocities. Boundary integral transforms express the formal partition function as an integral over constrained sectors labeled by complete local partial-Neumann data on an auxiliary hypersurface. Independent variation establishes paired regular subregion solutions as constrained instantons, with Lagrange multipliers supporting lapse and tangential shift jumps that accommodate thermal and rotational mismatches. For selected nonextremal stationary families with an asymptotic boundary, the constrained saddle action takes the form $I_{\rm constr}=\beta\mathcal F_{\rm gen}=\beta(E_{\mathcal B}-\Omega_{\mathcal B}^{I}J_{\mathcal B,I})-S$, with $\beta=T^{-1}$. Here $E_{\mathcal B}$ and $J_{\mathcal B,I}$ are renormalized Hamiltonian charges and $S$ is the black hole entropy, whose contribution to the action comes from the regular horizon cap. Interior stationary points of the landscape correspond to smooth equilibrium saddles when the retained variations independently span the entropy and angular momentum directions. We extend the construction to local, parity-even $f(\mathrm{Riemann})$ theories without curvature derivatives by retaining the complete auxiliary interface data. The same thermodynamic form follows with Wald entropy, without a small-deficit expansion. Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes illustrate the Einstein construction, while five-dimensional static AdS black holes in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity and the rotating BTZ branch of new massive gravity provide explicit checks of the higher-curvature extension.
papers.summary: This work develops a semiclassical path-integral framework that interprets black hole free energy landscapes as integrals over constrained instanton sectors, yielding a thermodynamic action $I_{m constr}= eta(E-Omega J)-S$ for nonextremal stationary black holes. The formalism is extended to higher-curvature $f$(Riemann) theories, with explicit checks in Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet and new massive gravity, offering a new tool for studying equilibrium saddles in holographic settings.

papers.title: Construction of Causal Set Propagators in $2+1$-Dimensional Constant-Curvature Spacetimes from Two-Link Paths
papers.abstract: We study a link-based retarded scalar propagator on causal sets sprinkled into $2+1$-dimensional Minkowski, anti-de Sitter, and de Sitter spacetimes. The construction is based on the squared link matrix $\mathbf{L}^2$, whose expectation value counts two-link paths between fixed endpoints. In the high-density limit, the dominant contribution localizes near the intersection of the null boundaries of the Alexandrov interval, and the flat-space normalization remains unchanged in constant curvature. The resulting kernels agree with the corresponding continuum Klein-Gordon propagators for a nominally massless scalar with effective curvature coupling $\xi_{\rm link}=1/6$. Since the conformal coupling in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions is $1/8$, this value is not a conformal-coupling effect. Together with link-based results in $1+1$ and $3+1$ dimensions, where the same coefficient $1/6$ appears, this suggests that the coupling may reflect an ultraviolet property of the link structure, reminiscent of the combination $(1/6-\xi)\mathcal{R}$ in local heat-kernel expansions.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a link-based retarded scalar propagator on causal sets in 2+1 dimensional Minkowski, AdS, and dS spacetimes, showing that the high-density limit reproduces the continuum Klein-Gordon propagator with an effective curvature coupling ξ_link=1/6. The result suggests that this coupling is an ultraviolet property of the link structure rather than a conformal effect, and it holds across 1+1, 2+1, and 3+1 dimensions.

papers.title: Geodesics of the five-dimensional Kerr-(A)dS black hole in closed form
papers.abstract: The Hamilton-Jacobi equation for geodesic motion in the five-dimensional Kerr-(A)dS black hole separates in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates, but the resulting first-order system has so far been integrated case by case, according to the real roots of the radial and the polar polynomial. We give the general solution in closed form. In dimensionless variables both polynomials are quartic, and a theorem of Biermann and Weierstrass then yields the radial and the polar coordinate as one pair of manifestly real formulas, parametrized by an arbitrary point of the orbit rather than by a turning point, and valid for timelike and null geodesics alike whatever the root structure. The time coordinate and the two azimuthal angles follow by quadratures that reduce to elliptic integrals of the third kind alone, and the affine parameter by one more of the same type. Along the way we correct the inverse metric and the radial potential as published.
papers.summary: This paper presents a complete analytic solution of the geodesic equations in the five‑dimensional Kerr–(A)dS spacetime, using Weierstrass elliptic functions to express the radial and polar motions in a single real formula. The authors also provide closed‑form expressions for the time and azimuthal coordinates and correct earlier errors in the metric and potential.

papers.title: The NLL/NLO$^+$ QCD spectrum from Higgs-plus-charm correlations at the LHC
papers.abstract: We investigate the high-energy behavior of observables sensitive to the production of a Higgs boson in association with a singly charmed hadron at the $\sqrt{s}=14$ TeV LHC, with light-flavored hadrons considered for comparison. Our reference formalism is the hybrid factorization at NLL/NLO$^+$, where the standard collinear picture is enhanced by the resummation of energy logarithms at the next-to-leading level and beyond. We present a prime phenomenological application of the next-to-leading correction to the singly off-shell Higgs emission function, as implemented in the multimodular JETHAD interface, a core element to test the stability of our high-energy distributions under energy-scale variations and to assess the weight of missing higher-order uncertainties. The resulting natural stability traces our path towards precision studies of Higgs production within high-energy next-to-leading-order QCD.
papers.summary: This paper studies the high-energy behavior of Higgs boson production in association with a single charm hadron at the 14 TeV LHC using hybrid NLL/NLO+ factorization. It implements next‑to‑leading corrections to the off‑shell Higgs emission function within the JETHAD framework to assess stability under scale variations and estimate missing higher‑order uncertainties.

papers.title: Local Measurement Theory for Quantum Cellular Automata
papers.authors: Tommaso Brambilla, Alessandro Tosini, Paolo Perinotti
papers.abstract: The formulation of quantum measurements compatible with relativistic causality is obstructed by the tension between the locality of observable algebras and the dynamical state transformations induced by measurement processes. We develop a local measurement theory for quantum cellular automata, lattices of finite-dimensional quantum systems with a causal reversible dynamics evolving in discrete time steps. Measurement processes are described by localized completely positive maps and organized into operational measurement protocols, finite non-adaptive sequences of local instruments distributed across the causal cone induced by the automaton local dynamics. Each protocol induces an effective measurement on the initial time slice, whose support is constrained by the causal structure generated by the automaton. Non-local measurement effects therefore arise through causal propagation and composition of local operations, rather than from primitive non-local interventions or instantaneous collapse prescriptions. We establish the corresponding spatial support bounds and characterize the resulting measurement architecture. As an explicit example, we construct a two-step protocol for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour qubit automaton which, for suitable automaton parameters, realizes a Bell-basis projective measurement on two neighbouring sites after coarse-graining of the local outcomes. Away from this point, the same protocol generates a continuous family of deformed Bell measurements whose entanglement and stabilizer R\'enyi non-classicality can be quantified explicitly. The framework thus provides a causally consistent operator-algebraic mechanism for synthesizing spatially extended quantum measurements from strictly local operations.
papers.summary: The paper develops a causally consistent framework for performing quantum measurements on quantum cellular automata by composing localized completely positive maps into finite non‑adaptive protocols. It demonstrates that non‑local measurement effects arise from causal propagation of local operations, exemplified by a two‑step protocol that implements a Bell‑basis measurement on neighboring qubits.

papers.title: Cosmological perturbations from localized sources: a gauge-invariant multipolar theory
papers.abstract: We develop a first-principles description of the linearized gravitational field of localized sources in spatially flat Friedmann-Lema\^{\i}tre-Robertson-Walker universes with arbitrary smooth expansion histories. The construction determines the complete retarded metric and the induced perturbation of the surrounding cosmic fluid from prescribed source stresses and a cosmologically stationary past field. It includes all multipole orders and accounts for curvature tails, through which the field depends on the source's past history inside the light cone. Generalizing the Blanchet-Damour multipolar formalism, we identify gauge-invariant mass and current moments together with a canonical cosmic fluid moment that determines an independent scalar response. This response vanishes in Minkowski and pure de Sitter spacetime, although curvature tails persist in de Sitter. The gauge-invariant multipoles are obtained directly in position space. This gives an exterior description without the nonlocal spatial projection through the source interior required by the usual scalar-vector-tensor decomposition. We also relate the canonical multipole metric to the standard variables of cosmological perturbation theory. The retarded construction requires neither a slow-motion nor a geometric-optics approximation. We define effective multipolar sources by truncating the moments of slowly varying sub-Hubble extended sources at a prescribed Cartesian multipole order, recovering the earlier quadrupolar and octupolar models in de Sitter spacetime. We recover the known Minkowski and de Sitter multipolar fields and obtain an analytical representation for gravitational propagation in the $\Lambda$CDM model including radiation.
papers.summary: This paper develops a gauge‑invariant multipolar expansion for the linearized gravitational field of localized sources in arbitrary FLRW backgrounds, including curvature tail effects and a canonical fluid response. It provides explicit retarded solutions and connects the multipole moments to standard cosmological perturbation variables, extending known results from Minkowski and de Sitter to ΛCDM with radiation.

papers.title: A new class of rotating black hole solutions endowed with a scalar hair
papers.abstract: We present new hairy stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions. These solutions belong to a subclass of Horndeski scalar-tensor theories, in which there is no non-minimal coupling to curvature. The full rotating solutions are obtained numerically using the Kadath library based on spectral methods. The metric does not rely on an explicit ansatz but rather on the use of a set of numerical coordinates. Black holes obtained differ from Kerr in general, and depend on a new independent parameter, a primary hair, coming from a linear time dependence in the scalar field. These solutions admit a Killing horizon like the Kerr black hole, but are non-circular, and break the zeroth law of black hole thermodynamics.
papers.summary: We construct numerically new rotating black holes with scalar hair in a subclass of Horndeski theories, featuring a primary hair from a linear time dependence of the scalar field. These solutions deviate from Kerr, are non-circular, and violate the zeroth law of black hole thermodynamics.

papers.title: Gravitational fingerprints of a black hole solution in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
papers.authors: Carlos F. S. Pereira, Ara\'ujo Filho, Marcos V. de S. Silva, N. Heidari
papers.abstract: We investigate particle motion, optical observables, and linear wave propagation around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity with a vanishing cosmological constant. The analysis distinguishes the conserved mass $M$ from the orbital mass $\bar{M}=M/\rho$ and isolates the radial deformation $\sigma^2=1-q/2$, where $q=\ell_2/(1-\ell_1)$. At fixed $\bar{M}$, the photon sphere, critical impact parameter, and innermost stable circular orbit retain their Schwarzschild values. Radial frequency ratios also preserve their Schwarzschild profiles for the same areal release and particle radii, while proper distances, infall times, and accumulated orbital angles depend on $\sigma$. For radial fall, the tidal eigenvalues acquire a factor $\sigma^{-2}$, and the instability exponent of the photon orbit scales as $\sigma^{-1}$. In addition, we examine light deflection in the weak and strong regimes with an explicit account of the conical asymptotics. The shadow comparison with Sgr A* and M87* exhibits a coupling degeneracy when the orbital mass and areal distance are set. Scalar, electromagnetic, and massless Dirac perturbations probe the physical metric, whereas a homogeneous axial gravitational sector with $\delta B_{\mu\nu}=0$ admits an exact Schwarzschild spectral map. In this sector, both oscillation and attenuation rates scale as $\sigma^{-1}$ at fixed $\bar{M}$. Third order WKB estimates agree with frequencies extracted from time evolution to within $0.7\%$ for the reported fundamental modes.
papers.summary: The paper studies a static black hole in Palatini Kalb–Ramond gravity, showing that many orbital and optical properties remain Schwarzschild-like while radial deformations alter tidal forces and photon orbit instability. It also provides WKB spectra for scalar, electromagnetic, and Dirac perturbations, confirming analytic results with numerical evolution.

papers.title: Analytic results for the two-loop renormalization constants of Feynman gauge QED
papers.authors: Gregory S. Adkins, Elias Mitchell, A. Volkan Turan
papers.abstract: The two-loop renormalization constants $Z_m$ and $Z_1\!=\!Z_2$ of Feynman gauge quantum electrodynamics (QED) in the on-shell scheme are computed using dimensional regularization. Analytic results are obtained for these constants. In addition, analytic expressions are obtained for their expansion coefficients in the dimensional regularization parameter $\epsilon$ from order $1/\epsilon^2$ through order $\epsilon^5$. The high-order expansion coefficients will be needed for future multiloop calculations in QED and will provide a useful check for multiloop calculations in QCD.
papers.summary: This paper presents analytic two-loop renormalization constants for Feynman gauge QED in the on-shell scheme, including high-order epsilon expansion coefficients up to ε^5. The results serve as benchmarks for future multiloop calculations in QED and provide consistency checks for analogous QCD computations.

papers.title: Boundary-Sensitive Quantum Order on Non-Amenable Lattices
papers.authors: Xingzhi Wang, Zohar Nussinov, Gerardo Ortiz
papers.abstract: We show that quantum systems on non-amenable lattices, whose boundaries constitute an extensive fraction of the system, host novel forms of bulk ordering with no Euclidean counterpart. Combining boundary-retaining iDMRG with an exact symmetry-fixing duality, we investigate $p<5$ state clock models on the coordination-3 infinite Cayley tree. We find that between the ordered and disordered phases lies an emergent intermediate phase with bulk order induced by an arbitrarily weak boundary field rather than by conventional spontaneous symmetry-breaking. This establishes boundary-sensitive order as a distinct quantum ordering mechanism defying Landau's spontaneous symmetry-breaking paradigm. The intermediate phase realizes a bulk-boundary correspondence in which the unpolarized boundary selects a specific ordered bulk state.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that quantum systems on non‑amenable Cayley trees exhibit a novel intermediate phase where bulk order is induced by boundary fields, violating conventional spontaneous symmetry breaking. This reveals a new bulk‑boundary correspondence that parallels holographic dualities, offering insights into how boundary conditions can dictate bulk behavior in hyperbolic lattices.
